stemMd: A cube is shown in an isometric drawing with equal scale along all three axes. Its vertical edge measures 24 mm on the drawing. What is the drawing length of another edge parallel to either of the other two isometric axes?
explanationMd: All cube edges have equal true length, and isometric axis scales are equal. Edges parallel to any of the three coordinate directions therefore have equal drawn length. This applies to axis-aligned edges, not arbitrary diagonals.

distractorRationale.d: Equal axis scale does not halve receding edges.
distractorRationale.c: This would confuse an edge with a face diagonal.
distractorRationale.b: Changing axis direction does not double the edge.
distractorRationale.e: The equal scale and equal cube edges determine it.
